A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Regularized Langevin Dynamics for Combinatorial Optimization. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original RLSA and RLNN benchmark results, regularization ablations, and longer-runtime comparisons on maximum independent set, maximum clique, and maximum cut problems.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and the longer-runtime experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The RLD formulation, RLSA updates, and RLNN architecture and training objective are unchanged. Appendix C contains the same code operations despite its new presentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three optimization problems on the same RB, ER, and BA graph datasets and scales, including transfer testing on large ER graphs.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, Figures 1–2, and Appendix B. Correcting the spelling of Erdős Goes Neural does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain identical splits, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, training settings, and inference budgets. Appendix B still compares RLSA and iSCO using ten times more sampling steps.

E4.justification: The LD step-size comparison, RLNN regularization ablation, training-curve analysis, and longer-runtime comparison are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains mean primal-gap curves and standard-deviation shading across test instances. Seed, repeated-run, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Objective values and runtimes in Tables 1–3 and 6–7 are identical. Figures 1–2 and the accompanying reported rankings, trends, and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–28, their assumptions and derivations, and the connection to normalized gradient descent are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, proofs, or corrections are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about escaping local optima, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration, training efficiency, and regularization remain identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning binary variables, broader constraints, and incomplete theoretical understanding.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, postprocessing, and code-access information are unchanged. Appendix C is reformatted without adding or removing technical instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. The corrected spelling of Erdős Goes Neural in Section 4.3 refers to the same work and preserves the same relationship.

P1.justification: v4 changes 'coordinatewisely' to 'coordinatewise,' corrects the spelling of Erdős Goes Neural, and renames Appendix C from 'Example Code for RLSA' to 'RLSA Pseudocode.' The surrounding narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix C replaces the numbered, syntax-colored listing with larger monochrome code in a shaded, titled box, changing its page break. Tables 6–7 shift slightly within page 15; other scientific displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes small spelling corrections and enlarges the Appendix C listing while removing line numbers and syntax coloring. These localized presentation changes leave the scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, with no meaningful overall quality shift.
